title: Deterministic rule-engine findings over one run's persisted evidence (D1)
description: clozn.runs.diagnosis_rules.evaluate()'s output: a fixed catalog of deterministic rules, each evaluated against ONE run's already-persisted evidence (context receipt, messages, influence map, finish/termination, and an optional comparison run) with no LLM involved anywhere in the evaluation. This is a DIFFERENT artifact from clozn.run_diagnosis.v1 (clozn/runs/diagnosis.py, an unregistered informal schema): that module explains WHY a single request was SLOW or CUT OFF from timing/journal fields (status vocabulary observed/not_observed/unavailable, one fixed handful of named findings). This schema instead runs a FIXED CATALOG of PROMPT/EXECUTION PROBLEM rules (conflicting instructions, omitted input, format mismatches, measurement-floor evidence, run-to-run drift, and more) and every evaluation ALWAYS reports one entry per known rule_id, never a variable-length list of only the rules that fired. Neither schema replaces the other; a future slice may compose both under one investigation view, but this schema does not read or embed clozn.run_diagnosis.v1 documents, and clozn.run_diagnosis.v1 is unchanged by this file's existence. Every rule that touches text cites a stable clozn.text-span-addresses.v1 address_id (clozn.runs.text_span_addresses, reused verbatim) rather than inventing a second addressing scheme; a rule whose evidence is a structured field (finish_reason, a token count, a differing setting) cites that field's dotted path and value instead. Every rule always produces exactly one entry in `findings`, discriminated by `status`: 'finding' (a detected issue, carrying severity/confidence/suggested_actions), 'not_observed' (the rule ran and found nothing), 'unavailable' (the rule could not evaluate -- a reason is always given, never a silent skip), 'pending' (the rule needs evidence that was never attempted for this run, e.g. no influence map, no comparison run -- distinct from 'unavailable', which means evidence exists but could not be read), and 'suppressed' (the caller explicitly suppressed this rule_id for this call). `suggested_actions[].kind` anticipates D3's clozn.corrective-flow.v1 action-kind vocabulary, which does not exist as a registered schema yet; this module OWNS the provisional kind names below until D3 defines its own, and callers must not assume D3 will keep them verbatim.

evidence_field.description: A structured, non-text field this finding rests on -- a dotted path into the run record plus the exact value read.

evidence_text_span.description: A reference into an ALREADY-BUILT clozn.text-span-addresses.v1 document -- address_id is the one stable, reusable identity; local_start/local_end (when present) are a sentence-level sub-range WITHIN that same addressed text, for a human reader's benefit, never a second addressing authority.

finding_status_entry.description: status == 'finding': a detected issue. The only status carrying severity/confidence/suggested_actions.

confidence.description: exact: read directly off an unambiguous structured field. pattern_match: a deterministic text-pattern rule with inherent semantic risk. derived: computed from a threshold/ratio over measured evidence.

other_status_entry.description: status in not_observed/unavailable/pending/suppressed -- never carries severity/confidence/suggested_actions (roadmap rule: omit, never null-pad a field that does not apply).

comparison_run_id.description: Present only when a comparison run was supplied to evaluate() -- omitted, never null, otherwise.

redacted.description: Whether this run's text was found redacted at evaluation time -- always computable, so always present.

rule_registry.description: The fixed catalog of rules this engine version knows, in evaluation order -- exactly the set of rule_ids that will appear in findings.

suppressed_rule_ids.description: Echoed back from the caller's suppressed_rule_ids argument -- a parameter, not a config file (config wiring is a later slice).

findings.description: Exactly one entry per rule_registry entry, in the same order -- a rule is never omitted from this array for any reason, including suppression (see status=='suppressed').
